title: RAGEN: Understanding Self-Evolution in LLM Agents via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
data_curation: Not a dataset-curation paper; the training 'data' is self-generated rollout trajectories from the policy itself. Four environments span symbolic (Bandit, single-turn stochastic; Sokoban, multi-turn deterministic; Frozen Lake, multi-turn stochastic) and realistic (WebShop, multi-turn open-domain web shopping) settings, with the first three minimal and decoupled from pretraining priors. Evaluation uses 256 fixed prompts per environment at T=0.5, up to 5 turns. Each batch samples P=8 prompts with N=16 rollouts/prompt and up to 5 turns/10 actions. Rollout-curation findings favor diverse initial states with multiple responses per prompt (best at 4 responses/prompt), moderate action budget (5-6 actions/turn), and fresh on-policy rollouts (Online-1). StarPO-S further filters, keeping only the top p% (default 25%) of prompts whose rollouts have highest reward standard deviation. For the SFT baseline, BFS generates 1,000 training and 100 test ground-truth trajectories.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. Training is a single RL stage applied directly to a Qwen2.5-Instruct base (0.5B for symbolic tasks, 3B for WebShop; 7B/72B in appendices) for 100-200 rollout-update iterations, with no pretrain->SFT->RL staging; SFT appears only as a separate comparison. The only schedule-like element is the Online-k rollout-freshness policy, where reusing each rollout batch for k consecutive updates shows Online-1 (fully online) converges fastest and generalizes best.
method: RAGEN implements StarPO (State-Thinking-Actions-Reward Policy Optimization), a general trajectory-level agent-RL framework. Unlike single-turn PPO/GRPO that optimize R(s,a) over prompt-response pairs, StarPO maximizes expected cumulative trajectory reward J(theta)=E_{M,tau~pi}[R(tau)] over full multi-turn sequences (observations, reasoning traces, actions, feedback), decomposing pi(tau) into token-level likelihoods for autoregressive LLMs. Each step emits reasoning-then-action (think...answer) structured outputs; rewards are trajectory-level (e.g., +10 Sokoban completion, +1 FrozenLake goal, WebShop purchase). It instantiates either PPO (critic + GAE, gamma=lambda=1.0) or critic-free GRPO (group-normalized advantages). The core contribution is StarPO-S, targeting the 'Echo Trap' collapse (reward-std drop, entropy collapse, gradient spikes): (1) uncertainty-based trajectory filtering keeping the top-p% (default 25%) highest-reward-variance prompts, an active-learning principle; (2) KL-term removal; (3) Clip-Higher asymmetric clipping (eps_high=0.28, eps_low=0.2), both adapted from DAPO. Response masking and bi-level GAE are also evaluated.
eval_metrics: Metrics over 256 fixed validation prompts (T=0.5, up to 5 turns): success rate (task completion), rollout token entropy, in-group reward standard deviation (behavioral diversity), total response length, and gradient norm (stability). Reward-std and entropy serve as early-warning collapse indicators; gradient-norm spikes mark irreversible collapse. StarPO-S delays or eliminates collapse vs vanilla StarPO across all four tasks; keeping 50% of rollouts avoids collapse entirely in FrozenLake-PPO. The 0.5B StarPO-S model reaches 20.70% (Sokoban) and 21.48% (FrozenLake), comparable to zero-shot GPT-4o (27.73%/26.56%) and Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (19.53%/23.83%) despite ~100x fewer parameters. Bandit generalization: 100% with reasoning vs 81.25% NoThink; counterintuitive BanditRev 67.58% vs 56.25%. SFT on BFS ground-truth trajectories reaches 74.6% Sokoban / 23% FrozenLake, beating StarPO-S (20.3%/21.8%). Best generalization at 4 responses/prompt, 5-6 actions/turn, Online-1 rollouts.
key_results: 0.5B StarPO-S reaches 20.70% Sokoban / 21.48% FrozenLake, matching zero-shot GPT-4o (27.73%/26.56%) and Qwen2.5-72B (19.53%/23.83%) with ~100x fewer params. Keeping the 50% highest-variance rollouts (StarPO-S) avoids collapse entirely in FrozenLake-PPO; default 25% filtering delays collapse across all tasks. Bandit generalizes 100% with reasoning vs 81.25% without.
evolution_note: Extends single-turn RL-for-reasoning methods (PPO, GRPO from DeepSeek-R1/DeepSeekMath, DAPO's KL-removal and Clip-Higher) into multi-turn stochastic agent training, alongside the 2025 agentic-RL wave (Search-R1, WebAgent-R1, VAGEN, ArCHer). It surfaces the Echo Trap instability and motivates finer-grained, reasoning-aware reward shaping and turn-aware optimization for long-horizon LLM agents.
